title: Head-to-Head: Nebraska vs. SMU Volleyball
text:
Head-to-Head Visual Analysis

Metric Comparison Chart

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Constructing stat comparison dataset
stats_df <- data.frame(
  Team = rep(c("Nebraska", "SMU"), each = 3),
  Metric = rep(c("Kills Per Set", "Blocks Per Set", "Digs Per Set"), times = 2),
  Value = c(14.10, 2.80, 15.21, 12.86, 2.73, 12.10)
)

ggplot(stats_df, aes(x = Metric, y = Value, fill = Team)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.6) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Nebraska" = "#D00000", "SMU" = "#003366")) +
  labs(
    title = "Nebraska vs. SMU: Per-Set Performance",
    subtitle = "Comparing Kills, Blocks, and Digs Per Set",
    x = "",
    y = "Average Per Set",
    fill = "Program"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )







Figure 1: Comparative Analysis: Nebraska vs. SMU Key Per-Set Metrics







Efficiency Scatterplot

eff_df <- data.frame(
  Team = c("Nebraska", "SMU"),
  HittingPct = c(0.284, 0.267),
  BlocksPerSet = c(2.80, 2.73)
)

ggplot(eff_df, aes(x = HittingPct, y = BlocksPerSet, color = Team, label = Team)) +
  geom_point(size = 6) +
  geom_text(vjust = -1.2, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Nebraska" = "#D00000", "SMU" = "#003366")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.250, 0.300), labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(2.5, 3.0)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Hitting Percentage vs. Net Defense",
    x = "Hitting Percentage (Efficiency)",
    y = "Blocks Per Set"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")







Figure 2: Efficiency Scatterplot Comparison

title: Final Project Plan: NCAA Women’s Volleyball Statistics
text:
Key Variables of Interest
The dataset contains thousands of observations detailing team performance and play-by-play actions sourced from Matt Waite’s repository and public data. The primary variables I plan to explore include:

Kills & Errors: Measuring offensive efficiency and unforced mistakes.
Total Attacks & Hitting Percentage: Evaluating overall offensive production.
Serve Receive & Digs: Analyzing defensive stability under pressure.
Blocks (Solo/Assists): Gauging net defense effectiveness.

title: Final Project Plan: NCAA Women’s Volleyball Statistics
text:
Exploratory Data Visualization
Below is an exploratory graphic examining the relationship between kills and errors across NCAA divisions:

library(ggplot2)

# Sample exploratory data
set.seed(42)
n <- 120
vb_data <- data.frame(
  kills = c(rnorm(n/2, mean = 25, sd = 5), rnorm(n/2, mean = 12, sd = 3)),
  errors = c(rnorm(n/2, mean = 15, sd = 4), rnorm(n/2, mean = 6, sd = 2)),
  division = rep(c("Division I", "Division II"), each = n/2)
)

ggplot(vb_data, aes(x = errors, y = kills, color = division)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "NCAA Volleyball Performance",
    x = "Errors",
    y = "Kills",
    color = "Division"
  )







Figure 1: NCAA Volleyball: Kills vs. Errors by Division
